text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures climbed confidently on Monday, recouping most of the ground lost on Friday and with encouragement coming from a recovery in the U.S. debt market. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.78, up 0.77 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Weak Nov PPI data causes robust bounce-back in gilts. March gilt future climbs 25/32 to stand at 109-22. Volume light as market still nervous after last week's volatility. UK base lending rates seen unchanged this week.The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-22/32, up 25/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures overcame a bout of early nerves to recoup a large proportion of Friday's losses and traders said the positive finish, which left the contract at the day's highs, provided a good platform for further gains. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.94 up 0.80 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds, futures were buoyant in generally firmer European environment, with gains of more than 70 basis points. Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said inflation was averaging 3.8 percent currently for 1996 and he noted in few weeks data would come out which would show whether Italy was going in the right direction. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.70 up 1.30 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries stayed moderately higher in late morning trade. Hopes of near-term easing dashed by Greenspan remarks. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 114-16/32, up 21/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.47 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese government bond futures ended higher on dealers' short-covering, which gathered momentum as Tokyo stocks extended gains in the afternoon, traders said. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 125.80, up 0.15 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market came to a standstill on Monday, with little expected to ripple the pond until next year, new issues traders said. "Its all gone quiet," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said. "Everyone started winding down a week ago and there is nothing very serious to be done before the end of the year."
"All syndicates have their eye firmly fixed on an early launch to hit the screens next year," he said.
Some syndicate sources said Argentina was expected to launch a jumbo mark bond before the end of the year with a likely 10-year maturity.
